title: How Our Skin Reveals the Link Between Insomnia and Fear - Nautilus
gist: Brief teaser on a PLOS Mental Health study of the link between fear and sleep; the available text only sets up the premise that insomnia and fear/anxiety disorders reinforce each other.

insights.claim: Insomnia raises the risk of developing fear and anxiety disorders, and those disorders in turn rob people of sleep, forming a self-reinforcing cycle.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Sleep interventions and anxiety treatment may be complementary.
insights.locator: Fear and sleep share a close bond

insights.claim: Insomniacs live in chronic hyperarousal, with fight-or-flight systems active even when there is no threat.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Physiological arousal is a candidate target for sleep-health products.
insights.locator: Additionally, insomniacs live in a state of chronic hyperarousal
